This state/province's religious penal code took effect 26 November 2000, prescribing 100 lashes plus up to one year's imprisonment for unmarried persons convicted of consensual same-sex activity, and stoning to death for married or previously married offenders. The state hosts the most active religious-morality police force in the country, functioning as a parallel arrest authority beyond the secular police. A foreign government's religious-freedom commission's 2019 implementation study used 173 religious-court cases from 2017, sampled from this state and two other belt states, to document operational enforcement; this state had the largest share.

The capital-penalty text, the most active morality-police layer, and the largest documented case volume in the belt together distinguish this unit: one belt state has a carried-out stoning sentence on record, while elsewhere the enforcement documentation is thinner.
